title: PNH High Command Visits Kenscoff, Orders Investigation Into Massacre Response
detail: Haiti's National Police (PNH) said Acting Director General Vladimir Paraison led senior high-command officials to Kenscoff on August 24, 2026, a day after Viv Ansanm gunmen stormed the town, meeting with local authorities and the Kenscoff police station chief. Paraison ordered additional specialized units deployed to the area and instructed the Judicial Police's Central Director to investigate whether the police failure to stop the attack reflected "complicity or negligence," saying "it is an obligation to protect the civilian population." The International Organization for Migration's Displacement Tracking Matrix recorded 2,647 people from 702 households displaced from Kenscoff between August 23-25, with roughly 77% taking shelter with host families, mostly in neighboring Pétion-Ville; two displacement shelters in Kenscoff's town center closed following the attack.

media.caption: Haitian National Police high command visits Kenscoff after the massacre
